answer: Each identity registers in a harbor registry and parks 200 credits as its nadir floor, plus a 30-credit fee. The floor is per identity, so the k-th fake still costs 200 parked plus 30, and 1,000 fakes commit 200,000 parked plus 30,000 in fees. A prism audit samples each identity at three unpredictable times; any snapshot below the floor suspends it, forfeits its fee and freezes its floor. A rented-floor rotation ring fails because rotating one 200 across identities leaves audit gaps. An honest agent parks 200 once, pays 30 once, and reclaims its floor on clean exit.
